verdict.rationale: Kit documents OAuth 2.0 (with PKCE, refresh tokens, and revocation) and API keys as two credential mechanisms, and the Kit MCP server explicitly lets an agent 'read and write to a creator's Kit account on their behalf,' implying credential-based agent access. However, there is no explicit documentation of scope selection/granularity (e.g., read-only vs write, per-resource permissions) for OAuth apps or API keys, so least-privilege scoping for an agent isn't concretely evidenced. Missing for 10: explicit scope/permission list for OAuth apps, ability to restrict API keys or MCP tokens to specific resources/actions, and independent confirmation of least-privilege enforcement.
